**Visual Analysis:**

- **Plant**: Sugarcane (long, narrow leaf blades, clumping growth habit)
- **Affected part**: Leaves (multiple, widespread)
- **Key features**:
  - Many leaves have turned from green to a pale straw/cream/tan color — diffuse, whole-blade yellowing
  - Newer/inner leaves retain green color; older/outer leaves are most affected
  - No distinct spots, streaks, or mosaic patterns visible
  - No distortion, twisting, or grassy proliferation of shoots
  - No obvious rot at the base

**Matching against classes:**

| Class | Match? |
|---|---|
| Brown_Spot | No — no brown lesions/spots |
| Grassy_Shoot | No — no proliferation of thin tillers |
| Leaf_Scald | Possible — can cause straw-colored leaves, but typically shows pencil-line white streaks |
| Pokkah_Boeng | No — no twisting or reddening of whorl leaves |
| Sett_Rot | No — no basal rot visible |
| Streak_Mosaic_Scsmv | No — no fine streaking pattern |
| Sugarcane_Mosaic_Virus | No — no mosaic (green/yellow patchwork) |
| **Yellow_Leaf** | **Yes** — systemic whole-blade yellowing turning straw/pale, progressing outer→inner leaves, classic for Yellow Leaf Syndrome (SCYLV) |
| Yellow_Spot | No — no discrete yellow spots |

The widespread, uniform straw/pale yellowing of entire leaf blades progressing from older to newer leaves, with no spots or streaks, is the hallmark of **Yellow Leaf** disease caused by Sugarcane Yellow Leaf Virus.
